name: Authorized private menu operation gate
phase: Discovery and specification only; implementation requires separate explicit authorization
architecturalPurpose: Add a separately typed lazy continuation gate to the existing single-admin menu service so future transport can establish authorization before reading private request bodies, without granting reusable permission or changing the 23-operation service contract.

startingState.head: b343297bed2f290c2c1e2ea1b684dabfac75b7a9
startingState.worktree: Clean before creation of this specification

discovery: FoodPrivateMenuService maps exactly the 23 FoodMenuRepository operations. It exposes no authorization-only operation; a dummy read/write would invoke persistence and is not a valid gate.

SingleAdminFoodMenuService already owns a private #authorize method shared by all operations through #run. This method awaits the injected resolver, validates exact resolution envelopes and canonical principal, and compares only the injected administrator.

FOOD-001D2 implements a separate FoodPrivateDraftOperationGate on SingleAdminFoodDraftService, calling the same private authorization method, awaiting an opaque callback and sanitizing callback exceptions. This responsibility transfers without importing draft-service authority.

FOOD-001J policy rejects before its gate; the body reader runs only in the authorized callback. Its controller operations still authorize independently. FOOD-001K exposes service and gate from the same concrete service, not a cast of a narrow service.

Menu H returns exactly service/workspace and J returns that same bundle. Neither currently exposes a typed gate. Runtime capability exposure is a separate prerequisite before real transport assembly, not permission to change H/J in K.

The E test currently requires exactly 23 concrete prototype methods and bans runAuthorized in source. Those two assertions must be adjusted for this explicit additive capability; existing 23-operation interface, behavior and all other isolation checks stay unchanged.

selectedArchitecture.decision: Follow FOOD-001D2: add a separate menu gate interface implemented by the existing SingleAdminFoodMenuService, reusing #authorize directly. Do not introduce an independent resolver/admin policy, companion service or repository bypass.
selectedArchitecture.input: One trusted zero-argument callback per gate invocation. No new constructor arguments: retain FoodPrivateMenuServiceDependencies { repository: FoodMenuRepository; callerResolver: SessionPrincipalResolver; administratorPrincipalId: PrincipalId } unchanged.
selectedArchitecture.publicSurface: FoodPrivateMenuOperationGate exposes only runAuthorized. FoodPrivateMenuService remains the unchanged 23-operation type. The concrete class implements both separately; the gate type does not expose management operations or internal dependencies.
rejectedAlternatives: A gate built from a merely narrow FoodPrivateMenuService cannot authorize without dummy repository operations or unsafe casts.
A second resolver/administrator gate duplicates policy and can diverge from the service.
An authorized mutation seam would bypass the required fresh operation authorization and is unnecessary.

construction: Keep the existing constructor and structural checks unchanged. Construction remains synchronous and I/O-free with zero resolver/authorization/repository/database/FOOD-001/body/network calls.

Administrator remains injected and validated canonically through parsePrincipalId, with no normalization, inference, defaults or hardcoded value. Existing fixed constructor TypeError remains unchanged.
No additional gate factory or new configuration dependency. No sessions, principal repositories or runtime dependencies are constructed here.
execution: Every runAuthorized invocation awaits the existing private #authorize method exactly once, fresh, before checking callback callability or invoking it.

Preserve E's own-key checks including symbols, canonical principal validation and all resolver failure mappings. Unauthenticated maps unauthenticated; canonical non-admin maps forbidden; unavailable, thrown/rejected resolver, malformed/noncanonical resolution or throwing resolution access maps access-unavailable.

Authorization-only execution makes zero menu repository/database/FOOD-001 read calls. Existing trusted resolver may perform session/identity I/O during execution; this is not a zero-identity-I/O claim.
On any access failure, invoke callback zero times. Denied callers cannot distinguish a callable callback from malformed input or learn record/payload validity or existence.

After successful authorization check typeof callback === function, then invoke exactly once with zero arguments and await its returned value. Never pass principal/admin/role, service/repository, request context or token to the callback.
No callback retry, cached caller/decision, shared mutable authorization state or permission token. Possession of an ID never grants permission.

resultModel.definition: export type FoodMenuAuthorizedCallbackResult<T> = Readonly<{ ok: true; value: T } | { ok: false; error: Readonly<{ code: 'unauthenticated' | 'forbidden' | 'access-unavailable'; message: string }> } | { ok: false; error: Readonly<{ code: 'callback-failed'; message: 'Private food menu operation could not be completed.' }> }>;

fixedMessages.callback-failed: Private food menu operation could not be completed.

resultModel.success: Return Object.freeze({ ok: true, value: awaitedCallbackValue }). Preserve the exact fulfilled value/reference without inspection, validation, cloning, freezing or reinterpretation. A callback's own { ok: false, ... } remains an opaque successful value in the outer success.
resultModel.failure: Freeze the outer failure and its error object. Access failures use existing fixed E messages; callback throw/rejection/noncallable after successful authorization maps only to fixed callback-failed.
resultModel.errorIsolation: Do not add callback-failed to FoodMenuServiceErrorCode or alter FoodMenuServiceResult. Gate does not return invalid-input, storage or configuration-unavailable as its own failure codes; such callback results remain opaque values.
resultModel.exceptions: Resolver/identity infrastructure failure is handled by existing authorization as access-unavailable. Catch callback synchronous throws, asynchronous rejections and await/thenable failures as callback-failed; do not propagate raw exceptions or silently invent successful completion.

freshMutationAuthorization: Gate authorization protects continuation entry, not a later persistence operation. Any mutation inside or after the continuation must call the normal FOOD-002F/FOOD-002E path, whose #run independently invokes #authorize again.

The two authorization resolutions are deliberate distinct checks, as in FOOD-001D2/J: first before private body access, second before operation input use/persistence. Do not optimize either away or claim authorization once for a request.
Revocation between gate and mutation denies the mutation with zero mutation repository calls. Any additional service reads or aggregate calls retain their own fresh authorization.

Do not expose an already-authorized service or unchecked operation seam, pass an inherited decision, or retarget operation arguments. All 23 direct operations remain independently safe without using the gate.
concurrencyAndImmutability: Overlapping gate calls each retain their own local authorization result and callback; resolve separately, invoke only the corresponding permitted callback, and do not serialize or share decisions between calls. Safety assumes the trusted injected resolver supplies the correct request-scoped identity; K does not claim to repair a wrongly shared resolver.

Follow D2/H precedent: do not freeze or clone the concrete service instance, its prototype or injected dependencies. The gate is a separately typed capability on that same class, not a separately frozen gate object. Result containers are frozen; opaque callback values are not frozen.
A future capability bundle may be frozen/read-only with service and gate referencing that same concrete instance. That exposure is deferred; no bundle field or runtime return type changes in K.
securityAndPrivacy: Keep private repository/resolver/administrator fields private. Expose no database, environment, session store, principal repository, principal/admin IDs, raw resolution or reusable authorization token.

Fixed failures must reveal no exception text, stack, config value, SQL/D1 details, submitted payload or private evidence. Do not retain callbacks or payloads after execution beyond normal promise completion.
Callbacks are trusted injected code and own their successful result contract. Opaque return preservation is not an automatic sanitization guarantee for arbitrary successful callback values.
K has no Request/FormData/body/parser/Origin/CSRF dependency. A future body-reading callback is not invoked until authorization succeeds. No body is read in K or this specification task.
compatibilityAndFutureExposure: Future K implementation requires a narrow additive seam in E's concrete class and tests only. Keep FoodPrivateMenuService, FoodPrivateMenuServiceDependencies, all 23 methods, five service error codes, forwarding, repository envelope validation, sequencing and E/F consumers/fakes source-compatible.

E's original no-gate exclusion applied to E's initial slice; K explicitly permits only this separate capability and related tests. Preserve all other exclusions, including no transport implementation.

Do not modify H/I/J factories, input/output types or behavior. A trusted caller constructing SingleAdminFoodMenuService directly can use it as both service and gate without assertions or a second service.

Preferred future runtime integration follows FOOD-001K: separately approved additive capability exposure through H/J using the same already-constructed concrete service for service and gate and retaining the existing workspace. Existing narrow runtime factories remain unchanged. Do not cast current H/J narrow output into a gate or create an independently configured second service.
Runtime gate exposure is a deferred integration prerequisite, not an implementation blocker for the two-file K extension. No further shared identity fix or domain/persistence correction is required.
futureTransportContract: Next expected functional slice is a separate private menu mutation transport/request boundary analogous to FOOD-001J. Specify any additive runtime exposure prerequisite separately before assembling it through H/J.

Future transport may reject method/origin/content-type/declared-size policy before body read. It then invokes runAuthorized with a lazy zero-argument continuation, reads/parses only inside that authorized continuation and dispatches normal workspace/service operations.

Denied gate means zero reader/parser invocations. Transport unwraps outer access/callback failures distinctly from opaque nested transport/domain results and provides sanitized feedback without payload echo.
Keep expected origin acquisition, CSRF decisions, payload formats/limits, parsing and HTTP feedback in the later transport specification; K neither defines nor implements those policies.
testObligations: Existing constructor is synchronous with zero resolver/repository/FOOD-001/body/network calls. New gate types expose only runAuthorized, not internal dependencies.

Unauthenticated/non-admin/unavailable/thrown resolver/malformed/noncanonical/extra-own-key/symbol/throwing resolution cases invoke callback zero times and repository zero times. Noncallable callback under denied authorization returns the same access failure.

Fresh resolver once per gate invocation; revocation between calls denies without cached permission. Concurrent deferred resolver results completed out of order do not leak success between calls or invoke denied callbacks.

Authorized sync and genuinely delayed async callbacks invoke exactly once with no arguments; async completion is awaited; values including undefined and nested failure results preserve exact reference and remain unfrozen.
Sync throw, async rejection, rejected thenable and noncallable callback after authorization yield exact frozen callback-failed with no exception/payload/internal leakage and no retry.
Gate-only authorization performs zero repository/database/FOOD-001 reads; callback-specific operations are counted separately from gate work.

Gate success followed by denied mutation performs a second resolution and zero mutation repository calls; successful mutation performs two resolutions and only the expected normal repository operation. Gate outer success does not reinterpret a denied mutation result.

Preserve every existing 23-operation authorization/poison-input/forwarding/outcome/error-envelope/pagination/immutability/publication/availability test. FoodPrivateMenuService and existing fakes remain source-compatible; callback-failed is absent from operation error vocabulary.

Adjust only obsolete concrete prototype/no-runAuthorized assertions to allow the separate gate, keeping management interface at 23 operations. Preserve all other source isolation checks; no draft-service import, body parsing, runtime acquisition or extra authority.

Use real DefaultSessionPrincipalResolver and AstroPrincipalSessionStore with injected async Astro-like session fake: delayed valid read gates callback, missing/malformed/expired/boundary sessions preserve cleanup, rejected reads yield access-unavailable with zero deletion/lookup/callback, cleanup failure fails closed. Keep existing sync/async destroy behavior and principal lookup/destruction regressions unchanged; no actual database is required.
Gate no internal enumerable exposure, no request/parser argument, no reusable token, no cached state. Existing H/J service/workspace outputs and construction purity stay identical.

acceptanceCriteria: Exactly this specification is created now; implementation is deferred and no existing file is changed/staged.
Future K adds exactly the separate menu gate/result types and runAuthorized on the existing concrete service using its private authorization primitive; no duplicate policy or unchecked mutation seam.
Fresh authorization before callback, zero denied callbacks/repository calls, exactly-once successful continuation, sanitized bounded failures and opaque awaited success are proven.
All direct operations retain separate fresh authorization and unchanged 23-operation interface; concurrent gate invocations do not share decisions.
Runtime capability exposure and transport remain deferred; body-read ordering is explicit without premature activation or request policy implementation.
